# Draft:Purple Parking

----
}}
Purple Parking is a UK-based company that offers airport parking and other travel-related services, including airport hotels, lounges, and transfers.
History of Purple Parking
Purple Parking began its journey in 1925 as a family-owned garage business founded by Jack Richard Inwards in Ickenham, Middlesex. Under the management of his son, Michael Inwards, the business expanded in 1970 to include a chain of self-service petrol stations that also sold convenience foods.
In 1987, Michael Inwards initiated Secure Storage Ltd, which specialised in storing new cars for London car dealers. Purple Parking was officially founded in 1990 when it started its airport parking services.
By 1990, the business was operating two sites in East and West London, accommodating up to 15,000 vehicles. That same year, Michael started a Park and Ride service from his Southall site, originally named Secure Parking Ltd, serving Heathrow Airport with just three buses and a small team.
This service evolved to include a Meet and Greet service by 1995. Soon after, the name was changed to Purple Parking and the company started selling airport parking at most airports across the UK.
In 2012, Purple Parking reported a year-on-year ‘Meet and Greet’ booking increase for airport parking services despite the UK still being in recession. Meet and Greet parking, also known as valet parking, involves driving directly to the airport terminal, handing your car over to a professional driver who parks it in a secure location, and then retrieves it for you upon your return.
Expansion and Partnerships
In 2007, Purple Parking extended service to 15 major airports in the UK, whose operations had previously been restricted to Heathrow. Major airports included Gatwick, Manchester and Stansted.
In 2012, Purple Parking became the official airport parking provider for Q-Park. The partnership offers Q-Park customers discounted parking at airports across the UK.
Legal Case Against Heathrow Airport
In April 2011, Purple Parking and Meteor Parking Limited won a High Court case against Heathrow Airport Limited. The High Court ruled that Heathrow Airport Limited violated competition laws by unjustifiably moving independent valet parking services from Terminals 1 and 3 forecourts to short-stay car parks.
Operations at Gatwick Airport
By 2017, Purple Parking's Gatwick Airport facility could accommodate 3,200 cars and handled approximately 70 arrivals per hour during peak seasons.
Administration and Acquisition
In October 2017, Purple Parking entered administration with debts of approximately £2 million.
Shortly after, Holiday Extras acquired the Purple Parking brand and website through a pre-packaged administration sale.
According to Matthew Pack, CEO of Holiday Extras, the acquisition aimed to ensure continuity for Purple Parking’s customers, suppliers, and distributors.
Recent Developments
In July 2023,  Holiday Extras secured a £20 million loan from NatWest, with plans to double its size over the next five years.
Current Operations
Purple Parking provides airport parking and additional ancillary travel services at Heathrow, Gatwick, Manchester, Luton, Stansted, Birmingham, Leeds Bradford, Edinburgh, Glasgow, East Midlands, Liverpool, Belfast, Newcastle, Cardiff and Southampton Airports. There are also facilities for parking at the seaports of Dover and Southampton.
